symptom: `$S = create M.Entity (Name = 'x', System.owner = $User);` (or `change $o (System.changedBy = …)`, `set $o/System.owner = …`) passed `check -p`, and exec refused it with `member "System.owner" on entity M.Entity is not a known association (and a one-qualifier name cannot be an attribute) — create the association first (`create or modify association System.owner from ... to ...`)` — advice no project can follow. Issue mendixlabs/mxcli#1612 (11.12.5) expected the member to be writable 'as Studio Pro allows'
cause: resolveMemberChange looks the qualifier's module up in its domain model; System's virtual model lists real associations (UserRoles, User_Language) but not owner/changedBy, which are entity flags — so it fell to the generic 'unknown association' branch. And there IS nothing to write: Association "System.owner" in a MemberChange is CE1050 "Unknown association 'System.owner'." for every entity shape, microflow and nanoflow
file: `mdl/executor/validate_microflow_system_member_change.go` (MDL-CHANGE01, project-free, exec-enforced; `refuseSystemMemberChange` at the create/change call sites in `cmd_microflows_builder_actions.go`, NOT inside resolveMemberChange)
insight: Measure before building what the issue asks for: the expected behaviour was impossible, so the fix became an accurate refusal. The first measurement LIED: one CE1613 (a wrong-case `System.Owner` row in the same project) suppressed all six CE1050s in that `mx check` run, so every row read 'clean' — a CE1613 anywhere masks CE1050 checks. Measure each variant group in a project with no other error, and distrust an all-clean result that contradicts its own sibling. Keep the refusal OUT of resolveMemberChange: list operations share it, and `find $l by System.owner = $u` builds clean (describe then prints it as `find $l by owner`, a separate round-trip drift). The working alternative for seeded/owned data is a modelled association to System.User — verified clean
